idiom_name: hand-written async trait + wrapper struct over tonic/reqwest (OnceCell lazy init)
implementation_notes: Nothing generates the delegate except the IDL client itself: define a trait with the operations the caller needs, implement it on a struct owning the generated tonic client (or reqwest::Client) behind a tokio::sync::OnceCell so the channel is dialled once, and translate transport failures with ?/From into a domain error type instead of an exception hierarchy. Result-based signatures make the failure contract explicit, and the trait is the test seam. The classic structure is still worth writing when you need retry policy, lookup caching or to keep generated types out of the caller's API.
pitfalls: The OnceCell caches the channel for the process lifetime; without reconnect-on-error (or tonic's channel behaviour) the delegate pins a broken transport.
Generated types are Send/Sync but interior mutability in async code needs tokio::sync primitives, not std::sync locks.
Mapping tonic::Status to a single domain error loses the retryable (Unavailable) vs permanent (InvalidArgument) distinction.
